built.helper: etagFor(buf) -> sha256 base64url, quoted, strong. Called inside the fs.readFile callback on the buffer just read.
built.ifNoneMatchSatisfied: RFC 9110 weak comparison, handles '*', comma lists, and the W/ prefix on either side.
built.sendFile: sendFile(req, res, filePath, contentType). 200 carries content-type + cache-control: no-cache + etag. 304 carries cache-control + etag and no body, deliberately no content-type. 404 path unchanged.

adversarialFindings.severity: material, affects how this item should be graded
adversarialFindings.claim: The dispatch and the WDLL both state that leg 3 -- a stale If-None-Match returning 200 with a full body and a DIFFERENT etag -- is the leg that catches a constant or hardcoded ETag. Measured, it does not.
adversarialFindings.evidence: Arm A above. With etagFor pinned to a constant, leg 1 still advertises no-cache and an etag, leg 2 still 304s on that etag, and leg 3 still returns 200 with a full body and an etag that differs from the stale tag supplied. The three-leg case passed.
adversarialFindings.why: Leg 3 compares the returned tag against the STALE tag the client sent, and a constant tag differs from it. The constant-ETag defect only becomes visible when the tag MATCHES and the bytes have CHANGED, which no leg constructs.
adversarialFindings.whatLeg3DoesCatch: A server that 304s on the mere presence of If-None-Match without comparing the value. That is a real bug class and the leg is kept.
adversarialFindings.disposition: Legs kept verbatim AND supplemented with two assertions that do fire: six assets must yield six distinct validators, and a file whose bytes change mid-process must stop 304ing its old validator.
adversarialFindings.processNote: DEV_PROCESS 3.2 -- reporting a planner figure as wrong is a successful outcome. This is that.
